transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 10:00am PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Alex (PM), Priya (Eng Manager), Marcus (SRE), Diego (Infra), Lina (QA), Samira (Design)

Summary:
- Q1 2027 launch readiness planning for roadmap items: Dedicated launch pilot, API performance improvements, and improved observability for rollouts.
- Decided on a narrow MVP for initial launch to meet enterprise SLAs while limiting scope for QA.
- Identified key risk areas: load testing, KV cache regressions with recent attention optimizations, and rollout automation gaps.
- Next steps and owners assigned for tests, docs, and cost validation.

Topics discussed:
- MVP scope and release date targets
- Performance validation plan (load tests, latency SLOs)
- Dedicated vs hosted capacity sizing and cost estimates
- QA/regression plan and release checklist items
- Postmortem learnings from last incident and mitigation items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we've got an hour and change, main goal is to lock scope for the Q1 pilot and make sure we have clear owners for launch readiness tasks.
[00:12] Priya: yeah, we need to be realistic — last time we tried to do too much and QA stretched for three weeks, so I'm suggesting we narrow to the three most impactful features: Dedicated pilot onboarding, improved prefix caching, and the rollout/observability dashboards.
[00:28] Marcus: agree, and from SRE perspective the big unknown is sustained throughput with continuous batching turned on. We saw memory growth on the KV cache during the last perf run. That bites into latency SLOs.
[00:42] Diego: that happened when we had mixed model variants on the same node; kernel selection churn made memory spikes worse. For Dedicated pilot we should probably pin model variants or at least reserve node pools. I'll do sizing estimates.
[00:55] Alex: good — Diego, can you confirm cost delta for pinned pools vs shared by end of next week?
[01:01] Diego: yes, I'll have numbers by 12/17.
[01:05] Priya: on the feature side, can we scope the onboarding flow to manual-config first and then automated templates later? That reduces surface area for compliance checks.
[01:14] Samira: from design, manual-config keeps the UI simple for the pilot customers. We can show the automated templates as coming soon and collect feedback.
[01:20] Lina: QA needs clear regression sets — especially around streaming responses and function/tool-calling; those are where we've had flaky tests. I'll draft a matrix.
[01:30] Marcus: and I'll run an end-to-end load test with a 50% traffic simulation to validate the canary thresholds. Need to decide what "50%" means — concurrent sessions or token throughput?
[01:43] Priya: token throughput is more representative given batching behavior. Let's define the scenarios in the test plan.
[01:49] Marcus: noted. I'll coordinate with Diego on the infra topology used for the tests.
[01:54] Alex: also security/compliance questions — enterprise customers want stronger audit logs and KMS integration for key rotation. Are those scoped?
[02:03] Priya: we will include KMS proof-of-concept for the pilot but not full HSM. The audit logs should be available via the console; Marcus, can you validate retention behaviour?
[02:12] Marcus: yes, retention is configurable but we need to test export and retention enforcement end-to-end.
[02:17] Diego: quick note — the last incident postmortem flagged two issues: an autoscaler bug that allowed nodes to drain without inflight request draining, and a mismatch in model variant compatibility checks. We've got fixes queued but need to prioritize them for the launch.
[02:31] Priya: can we get a patch review and staging rollout for that autoscaler fix ASAP? It's a blocker for canaries.
[02:38] Diego: I'll bump the autoscaler fix to high priority, target staging rollout by 12/15.
[02:43] Samira: from UX perspective, we should include a visible "degraded mode" banner so customers know when fallback happens — reduces support noise.
[02:52] Alex: good call. Add that to the rollout checklist.
[02:55] Lina: we'll also validate failure modes in regression tests — degraded UI, fallback model responses, and partial KV cache misses.
[03:04] Marcus: on metrics, we need token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and a tracer for kernel selection so we can see where time is spent. That will help debug the tail latency spikes.
[03:18] Priya: we'll add those to the observability ticket. Alex, can you prioritize the tracing hooks?
[03:24] Alex: yes, I'll add the ticket and mark it priority-high for the pilot.
[03:28] Diego: one more infra note — Dedicated cluster autoscaling limits need adjustment if we want to avoid cold starts on burst. I'll propose conservative scale-up thresholds to keep latency stable during ramp.
[03:40] Priya: okay that's sounding like our risk list: KV cache memory growth, autoscaler bug, regression test gaps, rollout automation. Anything else?
[03:49] Samira: we should also prepare a short runbook for support explaining fallback logic and how to escalate — keeps CS from being surprised.
[03:56] Alex: agree. Action item for Samira to draft support-facing one-pager.
[04:00] Lina: timeline wise, if we lock scope this week we can start QA preflight and run the first full regression in mid-December, leaving a couple of weeks for fixes before a late-January soft launch.
[04:14] Priya: sounds reasonable. Let's target internal canary by week of 1/10 and limited external pilot late Jan.
[04:22] Marcus: ping on benchmarks — we'll compare to the reference numbers we publish vs Anthropic and OpenAI for the common prompt sets. Need to ensure our cost per token numbers look competitive.
[04:36] Alex: marketing will want those numbers; Priya, can we get a conservative public-facing stat?
[04:41] Priya: I'll work with Diego and Marcus to produce conservative numbers by 12/20.
[04:48] Diego: quick reminder, kernel selection optimizations improved throughput but introduced some nondeterministic memory patterns in the earlier rollout — ensure that the load test runs multiple iterations to surface that.
[04:59] Marcus: agreed, will run iterations across variants.
[05:04] Alex: okay let's recap next steps and owners.
[05:08] Priya: I'll finalize the scope doc (MVP list) and lock it by 12/16.
[05:12] Marcus: run the token-throughput load tests and post results by 12/20.
[05:16] Lina: publish regression matrix and run first pass by 12/18.
[05:20] Diego: autoscaler fix to staging by 12/15 and cluster sizing + cost estimate by 12/17.
[05:26] Samira: support one-pager and degraded-mode UX by 12/21.
[05:30] Alex: I'll update rollout playbook, add tracing hook ticket, and circulate to the group by 12/14.
[05:36] Priya: any blockers we haven't addressed?
[05:39] Marcus: nothing immediate besides ensuring infra prioritizes autoscaler patch.
[05:44] Alex: alright thanks everyone. We'll do a quick follow-up on 12/14 to confirm playbook and again on 12/22 to review test results.
[05:52] Priya: noted.
[05:54] Diego: noted.
[05:56] End of meeting.
